$comment: OPT8 (plan 22) NEGATIVE PIN for the LIR peephole's redundant-copy rule. After regalloc most instructions have result == their only operand register; MEASURED corpus-wide, 12021 do at post-callconv and only 5575 of them are the register class's declared COPY. The other 6446 (zext/sext/trunc/not/neg/shl/shr_l/movaps/...) read a register and write a DIFFERENT value back to it, and on x86-64 `mov`, `trunc` and `zext` are three distinct LIR opcodes that all disassemble as `mov`. A peephole matching 'result is its own operand', or matching the mnemonic text, or matching the encoded byte, deletes live computation and still passes every structural check -- the program just returns the wrong number. Each of the four self-ops here owns one bit of the exit code (1 trunc, 2 sext, 4 not, 8 neg), so a wrongly-deleted one names itself. Inputs are `volatile` so ConstFold cannot evaluate them away: the `release` arm exercises the same four instructions as the baseline arm. exit = 1|2|4|8 = 15.
